items.stem: The debt service cover ratio (DSCR) for a period is best described as:

options.text: Cash flow available for debt service divided by debt service due
options.rationale: Correct: DSCR compares cash available for debt service to the debt service due.

options.text: Total debt divided by total equity

options.rationale: That is an operating margin, not a cover ratio.

options.text: Net profit divided by interest only
options.rationale: DSCR covers principal and interest from cash flow, not just interest from profit.

items.explanation: Correct: DSCR is cash available for debt service divided by the debt service due in the period.

items.stem: Which TWO features are characteristic of a project-finance (limited recourse) structure? (Select TWO)

options.text: Lenders rely primarily on the project's own cash flows for repayment
options.rationale: Correct: repayment comes from project cash flows, not the sponsors' balance sheets.

options.text: The project is held in a dedicated special-purpose vehicle
options.rationale: Correct: an SPV ring-fences the project's assets and liabilities.

options.text: Sponsors guarantee all debt with full recourse in all cases
options.rationale: Full recourse is the opposite of limited-recourse project finance.

options.text: There is no separate legal entity for the project
options.rationale: A separate SPV is a defining feature.

items.explanation: Correct: reliance on project cash flows and the use of an SPV define limited-recourse project finance.

items.stem: Why are debt repayments often 'sculpted' in a project-finance model?

options.text: To keep the cover ratio stable as cash flow varies over time
options.rationale: Correct: sculpting shapes repayments to the cash profile to hold cover steady.

options.text: To make the model easier to build
options.rationale: Sculpting adds complexity; it is done for cover stability.
There is no such straight-line requirement; sculpting is the point.

items.explanation: Correct: sculpting matches repayments to the cash-flow profile to maintain a stable cover ratio.
